title: fix(scripts): the objectui changeset digest reads a (breaking …) parenthetical inside a bold lead label
body:
Fixes #23118

Clause-②: no

## What changed

One file, `scripts/objectui-changeset-digest.mjs`:

- **`BREAKING_LEAD_LABEL`**, a new rule beside `BREAKING_BLOCK_OPENER`, which stays byte-identical. A line reads breaking when all three hold:
  - it opens with `**`, after optional indentation and an optional bullet (`-`, `*`, `+`), so the label is the line's first token;
  - the `(` sits inside that first bold span: nothing before it closes the span, and the span closes on the same line;
  - `breaking` is the parenthetical's first word, in any case.
- **`hasBreakingAnnotation`** tests the new rule on every line, not only at a block start. A bullet opens a line without opening a block: `- **Strict authoring face.** …` followed by `- **Tolerant face (breaking for invalid documents).** …` is a real objectui shape.
- **`markBreaking` / `OPENS_WITH_BREAKING_LABEL`: unchanged, by measurement.** See *Assumption 3* below.
- **Self-test:** a new battery, `#23118: a bold LEAD LABEL holding a (breaking …) parenthetical`, with 16 cases and a floor of 16. The roster floor goes from 17 to 18.

The rule follows triage's grade on the card: a bold span opening the line, holding a parenthetical whose first word is `breaking`. A `(breaking …)` anywhere else is prose, and so is a bold span that is not the line's first token. The line-start opener rule from PR #23117 is unchanged.

## Corpus reading

**Tree:** a blobless bare clone of `objectstack-ai/objectui`, with every head (1143 refs) and every pull-request head (7169 refs); objectui `main` at `45ae6b89e845`. Every blob ever written under `.changeset/*.md` (README excluded) was read from each distinct `.changeset` tree object and fetched in full: **6449 blobs over 4825 paths**. The heads-only subset is 5683 blobs; the earlier reading on the decoration card had 5678 at `main` `5595aabca30b`. Each body was parsed with the digest's own `parseChangeset` and judged with `hasBreakingAnnotation`: the base at `f931e765b` (blob `afaae0663b1a`) against this branch.

**Assumption 1 (reproduced on current `main`):** at `f931e765b`, `hasBreakingAnnotation(parseChangeset(text).body)` returns `false` for objectui `8a55f0ccd`'s `.changeset/12059-sidebar-no-reorder.md` (blob `873e53f906`). The positive control, objectui#12242's changeset at `1fb1ced36243`, returns `true`.

**Assumption 2, the split of the `(` blobs by position.** On the heads corpus, "breaking" right after `(` occurs in 39 blobs / 23 paths. That matches the earlier reading's 39 / 23 exactly, so it is the same set.

| position | heads | all refs |
|:--|--:|--:|
| inside a bold lead label that opens the line (**flips**) | 33 blobs / 18 paths | 39 blobs / 18 paths |
| anywhere else (prose, **no flip**) | 6 blobs / 5 paths | 6 blobs / 5 paths |
| **total** | **39 / 23** | **45 / 23** |

The 6 prose blobs are four shapes, and the rule leaves each of them unflagged:

- a label that has already closed before the parenthetical: `**Behaviour change on the console record page** (breaking in the objectui sense,` (`5896-feeditem-single-constructor.md`, 2 blobs);
- an unbolded plain-text label: `Narrowed (breaking for an author who wrote them, …` (`11168-element-family-inputs.md`, `11168-action-family-published-inputs.md`, 1 blob each);
- an unbolded code-span label: `` `@object-ui/i18n` (BREAKING; `minor` under this repository's release model …): `` (`11674-shortcuts-dialog-wired-only.md`, 1 blob);
- mid-sentence prose: `This narrows the accepted documents (breaking for a document of either shape).` (`11717-dashboard-widget-chart-measure-arity.md`, 1 blob).

Two blobs of `6152-unmirrored-round4.md` carry both a lead label and a wrapped prose line that opens with `(breaking for invalid documents).`. They flip because of the label. The prose line on its own does not read breaking: self-test case 4 pins that line.

**Flips (blobs whose verdict moves from not-breaking to breaking):**

- **39 blobs / 18 paths** over all refs; 33 / 18 on heads; 33 / 18 reachable from `main`.
- **Flips outside a lead label: 0.** Every flipped blob carries a line the lead-label rule matches. The other two rules are byte-identical, so no flip can come from them. Across the 39 blobs there are 41 matching lines with 18 distinct texts, and each is a lead label. Examples: ``**`@object-ui/layout` (breaking, declared `minor` per the version policy).**``, `**Narrowed (breaking).**`, ``**Retired (breaking), `@object-ui/types`.**``, `**Accept-set change (breaking semantics, released as minor by the version-alignment rule):**`.
- **Lost readings** (blobs the base reads as breaking and this branch does not): **0** of 6449.
- **Shapes the corpus never uses, so the rule does not admit them:** a lead label behind `__`, a heading mark, an ordered-list mark or a pictograph; a lead-label span that crosses a line; a bold span holding `(breaking` that is not the line's first token. Each has 0 occurrences.

**Assumption 3 (`markBreaking`), measured on the 39 flipped blobs:** none of them opens its summary (the first paragraph) with the lead label. So the `**BREAKING** — ` stamp lands on an ordinary summary in every real case. No rendered artifact below has a stamp followed by another bold label. `OPENS_WITH_BREAKING_LABEL` therefore stays as it is, and it is not widened for the hypothetical case either. A lead label names a package or a topic, not the class, so it is not one of the "breaking labels" the renderer keeps verbatim. The count note says "Each is marked **BREAKING** in the list above", and that is only true if such an entry is stamped. The self-test pins the decision (cases 10 and 14).

## Real hops: the count line before and after

The digest ran over the last 11 console pin hops, `0abd4f9f8769` → … → `1fb1ced36243`, plus the prospective next hop `1fb1ced36243..45ae6b89e845`, with the base and with this branch at `b7b8bf6d7`.

- **The current pin's hop, `7578323a544e..1fb1ced36243`, is byte-identical:** `→ 10 releasing changeset(s), 2 breaking (0 declared major, 2 annotated), …` before and after. No entry changes, because no lead-label changeset falls in this range. The prospective next hop is also byte-identical (1 breaking).
- **Two of the 11 hops change, and nothing else changes in them:**

`47b1f0bb7174..20c6d351ad74`, before:

```text
→ 33 releasing changeset(s), 6 breaking (0 declared major, 6 annotated), 0 release-nothing, 1 commit(s) without a changeset
⚠️ 6 of these carry a breaking change: 6 by the author's own breaking annotation in the changeset body — …
```

After:

```text
→ 33 releasing changeset(s), 10 breaking (0 declared major, 10 annotated), 0 release-nothing, 1 commit(s) without a changeset
⚠️ 10 of these carry a breaking change: 10 by the author's own breaking annotation in the changeset body — …
```

The 4 entries now marked are objectui `8a55f0ccd` (`12059-sidebar-no-reorder.md`, the card's example; its line now reads `- **minor** — **BREAKING** — The console sidebar no longer lets a user drag …`), `c7b30bd66` (`12063-unified-view-config-chart-retired.md`), `025341692` (`6152-list-view-legacy-chart-retired.md`) and `3fd862510` (`6152-list-view-readers-retired.md`).

`a58626c88dc8..f0268ad78485`: `173 releasing …, 4 breaking` → `173 releasing …, 10 breaking`. The 6 entries now marked are `5d77c099b` (`6152-list-view-options-bag.md`), `cf62edf68` (`6152-list-view-blocks-strict.md`), `b13ea3c67` (`6152-grid-default-filters-gantt-map-filter.md`), `1473757bf` (`6152-object-calendar-container-strict.md`), `d7e9e9ab6` (`6152-grid-kanban-calendar-17-7-members.md`) and `d73d98770` (`6152-resizable-columns-retired.md`).

`scripts/bump-objectui.sh`, `.objectui-sha` and every `.changeset/` file are untouched.

## Self-test cases (battery `#23118`, 16)

Direct, against the criterion and the renderer:

1. The card's example reads breaking: ``**`@object-ui/layout` (breaking, declared `minor` per the version policy).**``, in 12059's own paragraphs, with a guard that the fixture really carries the label.
2. The rule is line-initial. The second bullet of a list, which opens no block, reads breaking (`- **Tolerant face (breaking for invalid documents).**`).
3. A label alone on its line (`**Narrowed (breaking).**`), a label with text after the parenthetical (`**Narrowed (breaking), …**`), and the word in upper case all read breaking.
4. Prose `(breaking …)` outside a lead label does not: the 11717 mid-sentence line, and the round-4 wrapped line that opens with the parenthetical.
5. A lead label without the parenthetical does not (``**`@object-ui/app-shell`.**``, `- **Strict authoring face.**`).
6. A parenthetical after the label has closed does not (the 5896 line, verbatim).
7. A bold span that is not the line's first token does not (`See **… (breaking).** below.`, `**Removed.** **… (breaking).**`).
8. `breaking` must be the parenthetical's first word: `(non-breaking)` and `(not breaking …)` do not read breaking.
9. An unbolded label is prose: the 11168 plain-text label and the 11674 code-span label do not read breaking.
10. `markBreaking` stamps a summary that opens with a lead label. `**BREAKING (v17)**` is still kept verbatim.

Through `buildDigest`, in a fixture repo of its own:

11. Exactly the three lead-label annotations are counted (6 releasing, 3 breaking, 3 by annotation), and the three prose shapes are not.
12. The count line reads `⚠️ 3 of these carry a breaking change: 3 by the author's own breaking annotation`.
13. The 12059-shaped entry gets the marker on its line.
14. A summary that opens with a lead label is stamped once, with the label kept verbatim after the stamp.
15. The three prose entries are not marked.
16. A range whose only breaking entry is a lead label still raises the ADR-0087 disposition question.

**Every shape-1 pin of PR #23117 holds:** the `#23112` battery (16 cases) and the `#6099` battery (17) are unchanged and green.

## Ablation

Both legs ran from the committed `b7b8bf6d7` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. In each leg the anchor went 1 → 0 and the replacement 0 → 1. After each leg the tool confirmed that the blob equals HEAD (`2e67cb6c2848`) and that `git diff HEAD` is empty. This is a root script run from source, so no build or `dist/` is involved.

- **Leg 1, the rule's call site removed:** exactly 8 of the 16 `#23118` cases go red, all of them positives (1, 2, 3, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16). The 7 negatives and the renderer pin stay green, and no other battery moves. Self-test exit 1. The corpus census over the mutated module shows 0 flips.
- **Leg 2, the rule widened to `(breaking` anywhere:** 7 cases go red: negatives 4, 6, 7 and 9, and digest cases 11, 12 and 15. The census shows 45 blobs / 23 paths flipping, and **6 blobs / 5 paths flip outside a lead label**. So the corpus check can fail.

## Gates (at `b7b8bf6d7`)

- **Derived set:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on the actual change set derives 30 commands, identical to the dispatch's 30. All 30 exit 0. `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` ran detached: `✓ dispatch-gates self-test (fast tier): 1833 cases pass`, exit 0.
- **Reconciliation:** `--ran` reports `30 derived, 30 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- **The digest's own suite and its consumers:**
  - `pnpm check:objectui-changeset`: the digest self-test, 163 checks, `all checks passed`, followed by `objectui-range --self-test` (which imports `classifyRange`), also passed.
  - `pnpm check:objectui-bump`: `bump-objectui self-test PASSED — 20 assertions across 5 cases`.
  - `pnpm check:changeset-gate-self-tests`: check-empty-changeset 170 assertions, check-adr-0087-registration 548, check-changeset-no-major 401.
- **Lint**, a proven narrowing:
  - The population is read from `eslint.config.mjs`: the `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` object covers `scripts/*.mjs`.
  - `--format json` reports 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  - Every `parserOptions` in the config carries only `ecmaVersion` / `sourceType`, so no type-aware linting is enabled and this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch.
  - The full `pnpm lint` run is CI's.
- **Changeset:** none. Root `scripts/` ships in no package's `files[]`, so this PR takes `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, reported to the seat, not edited here (release text).** Two console changesets still pending on `main` carry the old rule's under-count, and they will publish into `@objectstack/console`'s CHANGELOG at the next release:
  - `.changeset/console-20c6d351ad74.md` line 43 reads `⚠️ 6 of these carry a breaking change`. The fixed digest reads 10, and 4 entries there are unmarked.
  - `.changeset/console-f0268ad78485.md` line 111 reads `⚠️ 4 of these carry a breaking change`. The fixed digest reads 10, and 6 entries there are unmarked.
  - The entries are the ones listed under *Real hops*. The other 9 pending console changesets read the same under both rules.
- **Further positions of the same family, outside triage's binding, left as prose.** The 6 prose blobs above are the four positions the grade rules out: a label closed before the parenthetical, an unbolded plain-text label, an unbolded code-span label, and mid-sentence prose. Two of them, the 11674 code-span label and the 11717 mid-sentence line, sit inside the pending hops. They are reported for the family card, not admitted here.
